sp.bc: Tiny dove-shaped flowers, 0.6–1 cm across: white to greenish white with a yellow lip, sometimes marked orange, with a dark purple spot.
sp.li: Bright, filtered light, never direct sun (about 15,000–23,000 lux). Good air movement.
sp.nr: Southern and southeastern Brazil, from Rio Grande do Sul north to Espírito Santo, in humid montane forest, often along rivers
sp.wn:
Growing season
Keep it evenly moist and water more while it's growing. Don't let the roots sit soggy or dry out completely.

Winter
An optional, gentle rest: water a little less, especially if your winter light is low, but never let the pseudobulbs or the mix shrivel.

Mounted
Mounts dry fast: in summer, water or mist daily.
sp.bn: Thin, curved flower stems up to about 18 cm, from late summer into autumn. Healthy plants can flower twice a year, in spring and autumn. Flowers last about 4 weeks.
sp.cn:
Easy miniature
A small clumping plant, up to about 23 cm, that builds into a specimen clump over a few years.

Temperatures
Warm days and clearly cooler nights: summer 29–31 °C by day, 18–20 °C at night; winter around 20 °C by day, 9–10 °C at night.

Potting or mounting
Grows well mounted on bark, if you can keep the humidity up. Or use a small, shallow pot or basket with a very open, fast-draining mix. Repot often, before the mix breaks down, and divide when new growth starts.

Feeding
¼ to ½ strength. Balanced or higher-nitrogen from spring to midsummer, then a bloom (higher-phosphorus) feed until late autumn. Feed less or stop in winter.
sp.ds:
A miniature epiphyte, sometimes growing on rocks, that roots into the organic matter collecting among its small pseudobulbs.

Also known as Ornithophora radicans and Sigmatostalix radicans.
